[32567 Business Intelligence for Decision Support | Subject description]
Credit points: 6

This subject delves into business intelligence (BI), a comprehensive term encompassing architectures, tools, databases, analytics, applications, and methodologies aimed at facilitating interactive data access and empowering managers to make informed decisions. It introduces decision support systems (DSS), which are computer-based systems combining models, methods, and data to tackle semi-structured or unstructured decisions, demanding user involvement and a user-friendly interface. As high-level business decisions often fall into these categories and are data-intensive, DSS are increasingly integrated with BI techniques for enhanced problem-solving. You'll learn about various aspects of BI and DSS, including group and intelligent support systems, web-based systems, decision optimisation, and personalised recommender systems. Additionally, the subject teaches the design, implementation, and integration of BI techniques to bolster business decision-making processes.

[32567 Business Intelligence for Decision Support | Learning and teaching activities]
Three-hour sessions per week of integrated presentations.

 The subject will consist of approximately 18 hours of lectures and 21 hours of seminar/workshops supplemented by guided online/offline discussion. These sessions may be offered on a weekly basis throughout the session or in block mode.

title: Learning outcomes
content:
[32567 Business Intelligence for Decision Support | Learning outcomes]
SLO1: Apply decision support models, methods and systems in related business intelligence systems. (C.1)
SLO2: Analyse decision models, decision methods, and decision support systems within a business intelligence systems. (D.1)
SLO3: Communicate technical knowledge through reports and presentations. (E.1)
SLO4: Collaborate as a team to meet business intelligence project goals. (E.1)
